data.one_liner: A Server-Driven UI framework for Flutter that renders JSON payloads into native widgets.
data.what_it_does: Stac allows developers to build and update mobile or web user interfaces in real time via JSON payloads delivered from a server. It uses a Dart DSL to write UIs that compile into JSON and render natively on the client at runtime.
use_when: You need to ship UI changes and updates instantly without going through app store review cycles.
You want to perform A/B testing or personalize layouts dynamically from a backend schema across Android, iOS, and Web.
avoid_when: Your application requires highly complex custom native rendering logic that cannot easily be serialized into JSON.
You need completely offline-first operations with zero network dependency for dynamic screen updates.
strengths: Instant over-the-air UI updates without updating the native client app.
Familiar Dart DSL syntax that mirrors writing traditional Flutter code.
Built-in network requests, form validation, and screen caching support.
weaknesses: Dependent on a backend infrastructure to supply the UI JSON schemas.
Limited to the prebuilt components and registered custom widgets supported by the Stac framework.
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing Stac in main.dart via Stac.initialize() and setting up server endpoints to serve the dynamic UI JSON payloads.
